q: The four priests received the blood of the victim in four jicaras, or bowls, made from the shell of a certain fruit, and descending one after the other to the courtyard, sprinkled the blood with their right hands in the direction of the cardinal points.
1883, Hubert Howe Bancroft, The Works of Hubert Howe Bancroft, volume 2, San Francisco: A. L. Bancroft & Company:

e: Uncertain. Probably a variant of juke (“to duck, evade, elude”). Compare also jink.

q: He has a set of four faux-bamboo drum stools made of jichimu, a Chinese hardwood.
2008 March 14, Wendy Moonan, “Rare Works by Eminent Britons”, in New York Times:

e: Borrowed from Mexican Spanish jícama, from Classical Nahuatl xīcama, apocopic form of xīcamatl.
